ground_truth_witness: Headline witness (4 vertices, G connected): G = C_4, the 4-cycle on V = {0,1,2,3} with E = {0-1, 1-2, 2-3, 0-3}. Take the bipartition S = {0,2}, T = {1,3}. Both induced subgraphs are edgeless, so G[S] has components S_1 = {0}, S_2 = {2} and G[T] has components T_1 = {1}, T_2 = {3}. The block C_11 = edges from S_1 to T_1 = {0-1} is non-empty. Recomputed quantities: delta(S_1) = delta({0}) = {0-1, 0-3}, so the proof says C_11 = delta(S_1) but here C_11 = {0-1} != {0-1, 0-3} = delta(S_1), with delta(S_1) \ C_11 = {0-3} (an edge from S_1 to the OTHER T-component). Moreover #components(G) = 1 and #components(G - C_11) = 1 (the path 1-2-3-0 remains connected), so "deleting C_11 strictly increases the number of components" is false: 1 > 1 is FALSE. C_11 is therefore not even a cut-set, let alone a minimal cut (bond). The same happens for all four blocks by symmetry. Smaller (3-vertex) witness for the equality half only: the path G = {0-1, 0-2} with S = {0}, T = {1,2}: S_1 = {0}, T_1 = {1}, T_2 = {2}, C_11 = {0-1} != {0-1, 0-2} = delta(S_1) (here C_11 does happen to be a bond, so it refutes only the "C_ij = delta(S_i)" half; the 4-cycle refutes both halves).
ground_truth_flaw: Step 3 of the proof: every non-empty block C_ij (the set of edges joining a connected component S_i of G[S] to a connected component T_j of G[T]) equals delta(S_i) and is a minimal cut (bond). A 4-vertex graph shows a non-empty C_ij that is not even a cut-set (its removal does not increase the number of connected components), and also C_ij != delta(S_i).
